text:
This looks like late 2012 to early 2013. The unemployment rate is 7.9%, which matches January or February 2013 (7.9% in both months). The fed funds rate is 0.16%, and the 10-year yield is 1.62%.

For the 10-year yield, 1.62% fits either November 2012 (about 1.65%) or January 2013 (about 1.9%), so the match is not clean. Unemployment was 7.8% in September 2012, 7.9% in October, 7.8% in November and December, 7.9% in January 2013, and 7.7% in February 2013.

The 12-month equity return of 20.9% fits the period ending October or November 2012 or later. Gold at -0.5% over 12 months and +3.4% over 3 months fits November 2012, though gold's 12-month change around then was roughly flat. The 10-year yield at 1.62% with a 3-month change of +0.05 also fits November 2012 (1.6% in August, 1.65% in November).

Headline CPI at 2.18% with a 3-month rise of 0.76 fits October 2012 (2.2% in October, versus 1.7% in July). US large-cap returned +0.6% over the latest month and +1.0% over 3 months, which fits October 2012 (S&P was about -1.9% in October and roughly flat over 3 months), and also November 2012 (+0.6%). The VIX at 15.06 fits November 2012 end (about 15.9) reasonably well.

I'll go with November 2012. The 3-month payroll average of 170k fits too. Unemployment published for November was 7.7%, but the figure here may be the value as first known (October at 7.9%), so that does not rule it out.
